items.item: AQE converts sort-merge to shuffled hash join too, not only to broadcast, when every post-shuffle partition is smaller than spark.sql.adaptive.maxShuffledHashJoinLocalMapThreshold — a third conversion this topic's own examples.py does not separately construct, since the broadcast-demotion case already shows the same underlying reoptimization mechanism.

at.out: the shuffled-hash conversion route named only; this topic's own measurement constructs the broadcast route instead

items.item: spark.sql.adaptive.localShuffleReader.enabled (default true) is what lets the non-broadcast side read its own shuffle output locally once the join becomes a broadcast join, avoiding a second real shuffle.

at.out: the local-shuffle-read config named only; visible in this topic's own Final Plan as the absence of any Exchange on the non-broadcast side

items.item: spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.initialPartitionNum, not spark.sql.shuffle.partitions, is the real starting partition count AQE coalesces down from when it's explicitly set; otherwise it falls back to spark.sql.shuffle.partitions, which is what this topic's own second example relies on.

at.out: the initialPartitionNum fallback chain named only; this topic's own examples.py leaves it unset and relies on the shuffle.partitions fallback

items.item: spark.sql.adaptive.advisoryPartitionSizeInBytes (default 64 MB) is the target byte size AQE coalesces toward, not a fixed partition count — a dataset far below that target gets merged into very few partitions regardless of how many were configured.

at.out: the advisory-size target named only; this topic's own examples.py measures the resulting coalesced-vs-not plan text, not the target byte size itself

items.item: spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.minPartitionSize guards against merging away all parallelism when the advisory size is ignored for parallelism-first coalescing, which is the default coalescing mode.

at.out: the parallelism-first default and its own minimum-size guard, named only

items.item: The reoptimization only ever rewrites the plan at and above an unmaterialized shuffle or broadcast boundary — AdaptiveSparkPlanExec's own bottom-up traversal only creates a new query stage once every child stage below it has already finished, which is the exact mechanism behind this topic's own 'nothing before the first exchange changes' claim.

at.out: the bottom-up, stage-by-stage traversal named and quoted; this topic's own examples.py measures its consequence (identical leaf scans) rather than the traversal algorithm itself

items.item: Skew-join splitting (spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled) is a third, separate AQE feature from the two measured here — it rewrites one skewed partition into several balanced ones rather than demoting a strategy or merging partitions, and is this topic's own handoff to the next.

at.out: skew-join splitting named only; deferred by this topic's own handoff to the next topic's lab

items.item: AQE's broadcast-demotion threshold, spark.sql.adaptive.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold, defaults to the same value as the static spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold but is tracked as a separate config — raising the static threshold alone does not change what AQE is willing to broadcast at runtime, and vice versa.

at.out: the two separately-tracked broadcast thresholds named only; this topic's own examples.py leaves both at their shared default

items.item: A cost-based optimizer with real table statistics (ANALYZE TABLE) can sometimes give the static planner an accurate-enough estimate that AQE never needs to intervene at all — AQE is specifically valuable when statistics are missing, stale, or the true selectivity only emerges from an operator the static estimator cannot see through.

at.out: the case where AQE has nothing to do, named only; this topic's own examples.py uses no table statistics at all, which is why its own static estimates are wrong in the way the Databricks blog describes

items.item: Each AQE reoptimization attempt is only adopted if the new plan's estimated cost is equal to or lower than the current one, per AdaptiveSparkPlanExec's own comment on reOptimize — a reoptimization is never applied blindly, even when it fires.

at.out: the cost-gated adoption of a reoptimized plan, named and sourced only; this topic's own examples.py observes the adopted Final Plan, not the rejected alternatives a cost check might discard

items.item: Whole-stage codegen, covered earlier in this chapter, is recomputed for each newly created query stage after a reoptimization, since the physical operators themselves changed — the generated code for a Final Plan's BroadcastHashJoin is not simply a patched version of the Initial Plan's SortMergeJoin codegen.

at.out: codegen regeneration after a reoptimization, named only, connecting back to this chapter's own codegen topic; this topic's own examples.py inspects plan text, not generated code
